codeFinding: GraticuleField.transform calculates normalized horizontal and vertical positions between source curves, then interpolates longitude125..130 and latitude35..40 linearly. This is a boundary-constrained angular interpolation, not the inverse of a specified map projection.
sourceGridFindings: 35N and40N are exported as mixed L/Q polylines and quadratic Bezier pieces, not analytic projected parallels with declared projection parameters.
125E meridian is a straight L segment;130E meridian is a sequence of noncollinear Q segments. The inspected export wrapper and grid placements are translations only.
Normal Mercator would have straight parallels and meridians; the actual curved parallels do not support declaring that projection directly.

Lambert conformal conic uses straight converging meridians and common-center circular parallels. The source mixed approximating paths do not establish those constraints or uniquely identify parameters.

A standard projection family could only be selected through an explicitly justified model plus independently held-out grid evidence. Approximate source paths with unknown drafting transformations and datum do not provide that identification here.

hypotheticalSensitivityOnly.model: Spherical Mercator one-dimensional latitude interval example, not claimed as source projection
hypotheticalSensitivityOnly.meaning: Matching the two bounding latitude curves does not make angular-linear interior latitude exact. A nonlinear latitude law can differ by kilometres within this interval.
hypotheticalSensitivityOnly.notMeaning: No claim that this correction applies to Seoul, Incheon, any source vertex or a DVA production transform.

identifiability.reason: Boundary latitude labels alone constrain their own values, not the interior latitude law. Without a justified projection family or further reliable grid evidence, multiple monotone interior laws remain possible. Source path approximation and undeclared datum further prevent a strict official-CRS inference.

existingResidualInterpretation.existingNumbersPreserved: Seoul about6.394km andIncheon about9.262km are comparison residuals under the recorded derived model, not isolated measurements of original source error.
existingResidualInterpretation.notAllSouth: The existing table has Pusan derivedlatitude35.13418 vs reference35.102, so the predominantly southerly residual pattern is not universal.
existingResidualInterpretation.pointSemantics: A modern city reference coordinate need not be the specific historic city center intended by an artistic source dot; that distinction remains unresolved.
existingResidualInterpretation.cannotClaim: Projection uncertainty proves the source historically correct or removes the registration block.

topologicalInvariant.finding: If the same one-to-one coordinate transform is applied to a native point and its source owner regions, the point-in-region ownership is preserved.
topologicalInvariant.consequence: Changing the geographic projection could improve modern-anchor alignment but cannot by itself turn the native Incheon city dot from red to blue. Native source ownership semantics require their own historical/time/scale review.
topologicalInvariant.exceptionNotAllowed: A non-injective transform, independent city warp, or different point/region transforms would not be a valid common registration.

minimalNextEvidence: Original cartographic projection/datum provenance or a reliable third labeled latitude curve/tick set that constrains interior latitude without city fitting
If none exists, preserve the vector source as unregistered/approximate with unresolved model uncertainty and do not silently replace the current transform
Keep geographic alignment review separate from source-native ownership and historical-time qualification
